summary: An eviction removes a loaded worker from the residency count before shutdown and does not restore it if the eviction is canceled.
scenario: With one available worker slot, a completed worker remains loaded. A spawn or reload starts eviction and pauses while checking its active-turn lock. The worker ID has already been popped from residents, so another reservation succeeds despite the loaded runtime. Canceling the evictor leaves that runtime loaded and the resident count at zero, allowing later over-allocation.

evidence.point: Capacity is computed only from residents.len() plus pending_slots.
Eviction pops before awaiting the manager, status, rollout and shutdown; unsuccessful eligibility and shutdown explicitly touch the resident, but cancellation has no rollback.
pop_lru_candidate removes the candidate from residents immediately.
The executed test pins eviction at the active-turn lock, checks the original runtime is loaded, cancels eviction, and observes the capacity state.

trace: spawn_agent_internal or ensure_v2_agent_loaded -> reserve_v2_residency_slot -> V2Residency::reserve_slot -> try_unload_one_resident -> pop_lru_candidate -> await active-turn lock -> concurrent try_reserve_pending_slot succeeds -> eviction future dropped -> loaded worker remains absent from residents

authority.source: residency.rs:105-115 capacity invariant and MultiAgentV2 configured worker limit

proof.name: residency_keeps_loaded_owner_counted_during_and_after_cancelled_eviction

proof.output: Summary: 1 test run, 0 passed, 1 failed. Assertion at residency_tests.rs:120 observed (true, 0), expected (false, 1), after confirming the first worker runtime was loaded.

severity: High: cancellation can leave a loaded worker permanently uncounted for the session, and overlapping reservations can exceed the configured loaded-worker capacity even before cancellation. It requires concurrent work or interruption at an eviction await.
